title_en: Guangdong Changjin Audio & Video Co., Ltd. v. China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianjin Tianbao Cultural Development Co., Ltd., Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd., Hebei Province Hebei Bangzi Theater, and Hebei Yinxiangren Audio & Video Products Wholesale Co., Ltd. — copyright infringement dispute
ruling_gist_en: 1. The preparation, organization, rehearsal and other activities of theatrical performances are all conducted by the performing unit such as a theater or troupe, and the necessary investment for the performance is also borne by the performing unit. The performance embodies the will of the performing unit. Therefore, with respect to the performance of an entire theatrical work, the performing unit is the performer within the meaning of the Copyright Law. full_text_en:
Guangdong Changjin Audio & Video Co., Ltd. v. China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianjin Tianbao Cultural Development Co., Ltd., Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd., Hebei Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, and Hebei Audio-Visual People Audio-Visual Products Wholesale Co., Ltd. — copyright infringement dispute

【Ruling Summary】

1. The preparation, organization, and rehearsal of performances of theatrical works are all conducted by the performing entity, such as a theater or troupe, and the necessary investment for the performance is also borne by the performing entity. The performance reflects the will of the performing entity. Therefore, for the performance of an entire theatrical production, the performing entity is the performer in the sense of copyright law. In the absence of a special agreement, an individual actor does not enjoy the rights of a performer.

2. Pursuant to Article 41 of the Copyright Law of the PRC, the rights of a producer of video recordings are limited to prohibiting others from reproducing or distributing, without authorization, the video recordings produced by such producer. As to video recordings not produced by the producer, it has no right to prohibit others from producing or distributing them. However, if the video recording producer enjoys, in addition to the exclusive distribution right over the video recordings it produces and distributes, an exclusive right to publish and distribute the content covered by such video recordings, then the unauthorized production, publication, or distribution of video recordings relating to such content by others also constitutes infringement.

3. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Regulations on the Administration of Audio and Video Products, when an audio-video reproduction unit accepts a commission to reproduce audio-video products, it shall, in accordance with the relevant provisions of the State, verify the commission letter for reproducing audio-video products and the authorization letter from the copyright owner. If the reproduction unit carries out reproduction without diligently and fully performing the aforesaid verification obligation, and the reproduced audio-video products infringe the lawful rights of others, the reproduction unit shall bear joint tort liability together with the producer and publisher of the infringing audio-video products.

Supreme People's Court
Civil Judgment

(2008) Min San Zhong Zi No. 5

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Audio & Video Publishing House, domiciled at No. 52, Dongsi Batiao, Dongcheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Pan Zhizhong, Director.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ruiming, lawyer of Beijing Zehe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xie Shufang, Manager of Management Department, Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Tianjin Tianbao Cultural Development Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 3, Fuyuan Road, Wuqing Development Zone, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Li Jianchen, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ruiming, lawyer of Beijing Zehe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Liu Xintu, Director of Hebei Xinyi Film and Television Production Center.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 3, Fuyuan Road, Wuqing Development Zone, Tianjin.

Legal Representative: Li Jianchen, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Wang Ruiming, lawyer of Beijing Zehe Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Xie Shufang, Manager of Management Department, Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Guangdong Changjin Audio & Video Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 3, 2nd Floor, Guangdong Audio-Video City, No. 118-122, Jichang Road, Guangzhou.

Legal Representative: Guo Jinglong, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Liu Hongliang, lawyer of Hebei Tianhong Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ge Huisheng, retired cadre of Hebei Provincial Radio and Television Bureau.

Defendant at First Instance: Hebei Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, domiciled at No. 52, South Jianshe Street, Shijiazhuang, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Xiaoying, Director.

Agent ad litem: Wang Guojian, lawyer of Hebei Bingye Law Firm.

Defendant at First Instance: Hebei Audio-Visual People Audio-Visual Products Wholesale Co., Ltd., domiciled at Xinhua Commercial Building, No. 10, Gongli Street, Shijiazhuang.

Legal Representative: Liang Riqiang, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Tang Cairu, dealer of the company.

Appellants China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Audio & Video Publishing House (hereinafter referred to as the Federation Audio & Video Publishing House), Tianjin Tianbao Cultural Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianbao Cultural Development Company), and Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianbao Optical Disc Company), in the dispute over copyright infringement with Appellee Guangdong Changjin Audio & Video Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changjin Company) and Defendants at First Instance Hebei Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater (hereinafter referred to as Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater) and Hebei Audio-Visual People Audio-Visual Products Wholesale Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Audio-Visual People Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2007) Ji Min San Chu Zi No. 1-1 rendered by the Hebei High People's Court on December 15, 2007, and appealed to this Court. After accepting the case on June 15, 2008, this Court lawfully formed a collegial panel and held a public hearing on July 29, 2008. The agents ad litem of the Appellants Wang Ruiming and Xie Shufang (for the Federation Audio & Video Publishing House), Wang Ruiming (for Tianbao Cultural Development Company), Wang Ruiming and Xie Shufang (for Tianbao Optical Disc Company), the agents ad litem of the Appellee Changjin Company Liu Hongliang and Ge Huisheng, and the agents ad litem of the Defendants at First Instance Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater (Wang Guojian) and Audio-Visual People Company (Tang Cairu) appeared in court to participate in the proceedings. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance found the following facts:

On January 18, 1998, Hebei Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House (hereinafter referred to as Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House) issued an authorization letter, authorizing Changjin Company to represent it in soliciting programs from literary and artistic groups or individuals holding copyright authorization, for the purpose of publishing audio-video products such as VCDs. The purchased programs, after passing review, were to be included in the publishing plan of the publishing house. On April 21, 2003, and December 6, 2004, Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House (Party A) and Changjin Company (Party B) entered into agreements stipulating that the parties would cooperate in publishing and distributing audio-video products, with Party B organizing the program sources, Party A publishing, and Party B enjoying the permanent distribution right over the audio-video products published by Party A. On September 11, 2000, October 9, 2001, May 21, 2004, and December 1, 2006, based on several contracts signed with Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater and the authorization letter issued by Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, Changjin Company obtained the exclusive right to publish and distribute audio-video products of the theater's performances, including the works "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" (Double Regret and Hatred), "Da Jin Zhuan" (Striking the Gold Brick), "San Da Tao San Chun" (Three Beats on Tao Sanchun), "Hu Die Bei" (Butterfly Cup, Parts 1 and 2), and "Chen San Liang". On April 2, 2001, Shijiazhuang Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe (Party A) and Changjin Company (Party B) entered into an agreement stipulating that Party B would record Party A's performance of the work "Qing Feng Ting" (Pavilion of Cool Breeze) and other works, and after the recording was completed, Party B would pay Party A a one-time usage fee of RMB 20,000, and Party B would enjoy the exclusive audio-video publication and distribution right over such performance works. On September 29, 2001, Baoding Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe (Party A) issued an authorization letter granting Changjin Company the exclusive right to publish and distribute audio-video products of its performance works, including "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" (Blood Stains Twin Plums). On October 3, 2001, Hengshui Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe (Party A) and Changjin Company (Party B) entered into an "Audio-Video Publishing Contract" stipulating that Party A granted Party B the exclusive right to publish and distribute audio-video products of the performance work "Chun Cao Chuang Tang" (Spring Grass Daring to Enter the Hall).

Regarding the audio-video products of the above performance works distributed by Changjin Company, based on the performance script of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater from July 1981 and relevant evidence, the literary compilers of the script for "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2) were Zhang Te and Wang Changyan, employees of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, and the music compiler was Zhang Zhanwei, an employee of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater. On October 29, 1999, Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House paid a usage fee of RMB 100 to Zhang Yi, the successor of Zhang Te. On August 10, 2005, Wang Qingchen, the successor of Wang Changyan, licensed Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House and Changjin Company to use the script of "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2) and to publish and distribute audio-video products of such performance work. The script of "Chen San Liang" was compiled by Wang Huanting, a former employee of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater. On March 12, 1998, and August 8, 2005, Wang Jingci (Party A), successor of Wang Huanting, entered into agreements with Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House and Changjin Company (Party B), stipulating that Party A licensed Party B to use the script of "Chen San Liang" and to publish and distribute audio-video products of such performance work. The literary part of the script of "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" was compiled by Shang Xianzhi, an externally hired person of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, and the music part was compiled by Zhang Zhanwei, an employee of the theater. On December 21, 2000, Zhang Zhanwei received a usage fee of RMB 4,000 from Changjin Company. The script of "Qing Feng Ting" was compiled by Shang Xianzhi, an externally hired person of Shijiazhuang Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe. In July 2002, Shang Xianzhi issued an authorization letter, licensing Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House to use the scripts of "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" and "Qing Feng Ting" and to publish and distribute audio-video products.

Among the above audio-video products, "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" and "Qing Feng Ting" were recorded by Changjin Company; "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2) and "Chen San Liang" were recorded by Hebei Television Station; "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" was a real-scene opera film shot in 1997, with the producer and performing entity both being Baoding Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe. Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House and Changjin Company obtained the right to publish and distribute audio-video products of the performance works "Hu Die Bei", "Chen San Liang", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" from Hebei Television Station and Baoding Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe.

The literary and music compilers of the script of "Da Jin Zhuan" were Zhao Mingqi and Ma Quangui, employees of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater. The literary part of the script of "San Da Tao San Chun" was compiled by Wu Zuguang, an externally hired person of Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, and the music part was compiled by Xu Huibao, an employee of the theater. Changjin Company did not obtain authorization from the literary and music compilers of the scripts of "Da Jin Zhuan" and "San Da Tao San Chun". For "Chun Cao Chuang Tang", authorization was obtained only from the performing entity and the script compiler, but not from the producer of the audio-video products.

On January 4, 2006, the General Editorial Office of Hebei Television Station (Party A) and Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater (Party B) entered into an agreement stipulating that the parties confirmed that the right of performers in the Hebei Bangzi opera performances recorded by Party A and performed by Party B belonged to Party B, with Party A being the producer of the audio-video products; Party A was not to license any third party to reproduce, publish, or distribute audio-video products of the performances recorded by Party A; and Party A licensed Party B the exclusive right to reproduce, publish, and distribute such audio-video products.

Among the audio-video products of the five performance works "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", "Qing Feng Ting", "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2), "Chen San Liang", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" published, reproduced, and distributed by the Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianbao Optical Disc Company, and Tianbao Cultural Development Company, "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2) was from the same edition as the audio-video products distributed by Changjin Company, and had obtained authorization from six principal actors including Zhang Huiyun; "Chen San Liang", "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", "Qing Feng Ting", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" were from different editions from those distributed by Changjin Company, belonging to performances of the same performing entity at different sessions. The performance work "Chen San Liang" was recorded by Hebei Television Station and obtained authorization from principal actors Zhang Huiyun and Tian Chunniao; "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" was recorded by Hebei Xinyi Film and Television Production Center and obtained authorization from principal actor Zhang Huiyun; "Qing Feng Ting" was recorded by Hebei Xinyi Film and Television Production Center and obtained authorization from principal actors Lei Baochun and Li Xiguo. On June 1, 2004, Shang Xianzhi (Party A) entered into an agreement with Hebei Xinyi Film and Television Production Center and Tianbao Cultural Development Company (Party B), granting Party B the exclusive right to use the scripts of "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" and "Qing Feng Ting". "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" was a recording of the stage performance version. The Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianbao Optical Disc Company, and Tianbao Cultural Development Company claimed that the performance was organized by Hebei Television Station and that they had obtained authorization from the music script compiler Liu Yunhe and four principal actors including Wu Tao.

Audio-Visual People Company, as a distributor, provided the sales authorization letter and sales detail list issued to it by Tianbao Cultural Development Company to prove the legality of its source of goods.

On June 15, 2007, Changjin Company filed the initial complaint, alleging: Since 2000, it had obtained from Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, Hengshui Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe, Shijiazhuang Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe, and Baoding Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe the exclusive right to publish and distribute audio-video products of eight Hebei Bangzi opera performance works, including "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2), "Chen San Liang", "San Da Tao San Chun", "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", "Da Jin Zhuan", "Chun Cao Chuang Tang", "Qing Feng Ting", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei". Around the end of 2004, Changjin Company discovered that the above audio-video products published by the Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, reproduced by Tianbao Optical Disc Company, distributed by Tianbao Cultural Development Company, and sold by Audio-Visual People Company infringed on Changjin Company's lawful rights and interests. It requested that the court order the infringers to cease infringement, destroy the infringing products, and compensate Changjin Company for losses of RMB 450,000.

The court of first instance held: The right claimed by Changjin Company is the exclusive distribution right over the audio-video products of the involved opera works. To legally publish audio-video products of operas, the publisher must itself own the copyright in the opera works, the performers' rights, and the video producers' rights, or obtain authorization from the holders of such rights. Opera works refer to dramatic scripts for stage performance, including the two parts mainly composed of lines and music as recorded in text and music. Traditional opera works that have entered the public domain may be freely used by others. Works arising from the adaptation or compilation of traditional opera works have copyright enjoyed by the adapters and compilers. Works created by a citizen in the course of performing the tasks assigned by a legal person or other organization are works made for hire. The compilation of the texts and music of the involved scripts by Zhang Te, Wang Changyan, Zhang Zhanwei, Zhao Mingqi, Ma Quangui, Wang Huanting, and Xu Huibao all constituted acts performed to accomplish the work tasks of their respective units, and therefore the works compiled by them are works made for hire, with copyright belonging to the compilers in accordance with law. The scripts of "San Da Tao San Chun" compiled by externally hired Wu Zuguang and the scripts of "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" and "Qing Feng Ting" compiled by externally hired Shang Xianzhi are works compiled under commission. As the commissioning parties did not agree with Wu Zuguang and Shang Xianzhi on the ownership of copyright in the scripts, Wu Zuguang and Shang Xianzhi enjoy copyright in the comissioned scripts in accordance with law.

As to the performance works in the audio-video products involved distributed by Changjin Company, the necessary investment was provided by the performing entity, the organization and rehearsal of the performances were all conducted by the performing entity, the performers and staff participating in the performances all acted in the performance of their duties, the performances reflected the will of the performing entity, and external liability was also borne by the performing entity. Therefore, for the performance of an entire opera, the rights to license others to broadcast live or publicly transmit, to produce audio-video products and to reproduce and distribute them, and to communicate to the public via information networks and to receive remuneration therefor, should reasonably be enjoyed by the performing entity. No individual actor enjoys the above rights over the entire opera, nor may they affect the exercise of such rights by the performing entity. The agreement between Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater and the General Editorial Office of Hebei Television Station confirmed that Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater had the right to use the audio-video products of all operas performed by Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater and recorded by Hebei Television Station, including the right to authorize others to independently reproduce, publish, and distribute the involved audio-video products. Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater stated in court that Changjin Company's distribution of the involved audio-video products was lawful, indicating that it had sub-licensed the authorization from Hebei Television Station to Changjin Company.

The audio-video products of the performance works "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2), "Chen San Liang", "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", "Qing Feng Ting", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" published and distributed by Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House and Changjin Company all obtained authorization from the relevant script copyright owners, performing entities, and video producers. Changjin Company enjoys the exclusive publication and distribution right over the audio-video products of the above five performance works. Pursuant to the cooperation agreement between Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House and Changjin Company, the authorization obtained by Changjin Company was naturally enjoyed by Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House. Therefore, the publication and distribution of the involved audio-video products by Bailing Audio & Video Publishing House and Changjin Company was lawful. As to the three performance works "Da Jin Zhuan", "San Da Tao San Chun", and "Chun Cao Chuang Tang", because Changjin Company did not obtain complete authorization, it is not entitled to claim infringement of its audio-video product distribution right by others.

The four audio-video products "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2), "Chen San Liang", "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", and "Qing Feng Ting" published, reproduced, and distributed by the Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianbao Optical Disc Company, and Tianbao Cultural Development Company did not obtain permission from the performing entity, constituting incomplete authorization; the audio-video product "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" published, reproduced, and distributed by them did not obtain authorization from the performing entity. Although this work was a recording of the stage scene, different from a recording of the real-scene film, the actor lineup and performance content were the same, making the two substantially identical. The Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianbao Optical Disc Company, and Tianbao Cultural Development Company infringed Changjin Company's exclusive distribution right over the audio-video products of the five performance works "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2), "Chen San Liang", "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", "Qing Feng Ting", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei", and shall bear civil liability to cease the infringement and compensate for losses. As to the amount of compensation, it shall be determined discretionarily based on factors such as the type of work, the nature and consequences of the infringement, and the reasonable expenses incurred by Changjin Company to stop the infringement. Audio-Visual People Company provided evidence of the lawful source of its goods, and therefore should not bear compensation liability, but shall bear the legal liability to cease sales and destroy the infringing products. Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater did not engage in any act infringing Changjin Company's exclusive distribution right over audio-video products, and the claims of Changjin Company against Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater are not sustained. Pursuant to Article 134, Paragraph 1, Items (1) and (7) of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC; Articles 46(11), 48, and 52 of the Copyright Law of the PRC; and Articles 19 and 25 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Disputes over Copyright, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. The Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianbao Optical Disc Company, and Tianbao Cultural Development Company shall immediately cease publishing, reproducing, and distributing the involved audio-video products of "Hu Die Bei" (Parts 1 and 2), "Chen San Liang", "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen", "Qing Feng Ting", and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei", and destroy the unsold audio-video products of the above works; 2. Audio-Visual People Company shall immediately cease selling the above audio-video products and destroy the unsold audio-video products of the above works; 3. The Federation Audio & Video Publishing House, Tianbao Optical Disc Company, and Tianbao Cultural Development Company shall, within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment, jointly and severally compensate Changjin Company for economic losses in the amount of RMB 300,000; 4. All other claims of Changjin Company are rejected.

The appellants, Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, jointly appealed to this Court within the statutory period, stating: 1. The first-instance judgment erred in finding that the appellants infringed Changjin Company's exclusive distribution right for the four programs "Chen Sanliang," "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen" (Double Mistakes and Lingering Hatred), "Qingfengting" (Pavilion of Clear Breeze), and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei" (Blood-Stained Twin Plum Blossoms), despite having found that the video recordings of these four programs were of different versions. According to Article 41 of the Copyright Law, the basis for enjoying the rights of a video producer is that the video recording was produced by that producer. The version published and distributed by the appellants was not produced by Changjin Company, so Changjin Company cannot claim rights over that version, and the appellants naturally could not have infringed any of its rights. 2. Changjin Company did not obtain permission from the copyright owner of the singing melody of the opera "Butterfly Cup," nor did it legally obtain authorization from the video producer, Hebei Television Station. There is no evidence to show that the General Editorial Office of Hebei Television Station had obtained signed authorization from Hebei Television Station. The authorization obtained by Changjin Company was incomplete; therefore, it does not enjoy the exclusive distribution right for the video recording of that opera, and the appellants naturally did not infringe its rights. 3. Even if the appellants should bear liability, the amount of 300,000 yuan awarded in the first-instance judgment is unreasonable. In summary, the appellants request that the original judgment be vacated and that the judgment be amended to hold that the appellants bear no liability for infringement.

The appellant Tianbao Optical Disc Company, dissatisfied with the original judgment, appealed to this Court within the statutory period, stating: First, Changjin Company does not have lawful rights over the video recordings of the five operas, including "Butterfly Cup," that the appellant reproduced, and thus the appellant cannot have infringed. Second, even if Changjin Company enjoyed the exclusive distribution right over the above video recordings, the appellant's act of reproduction could not have infringed its distribution right because the appellant's act of reproduction was a contract for processing and undertaking, which does not constitute an act of infringement of another's copyright. Third, the appellant reproduced the discs in question upon the commission of Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House, and Article 4 of the "Commission for Reproduction of Audio-Visual Recordings" signed with it clearly stipulates: "The publishing unit bears full legal responsibility for the content and copyright relations of the audio-visual recordings entrusted for reproduction." This "Commission for Reproduction" was signed in accordance with the requirements of the "Regulations on the Administration of Audio-Visual Products," and is not merely a contract between the parties. Finally, the appellant fulfilled the obligations under Article 23 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Audio-Visual Products" in its act of reproduction, verified all procedures, and had no subjective fault, and thus should not bear any legal liability. In summary, the appellant requests that the original judgment be vacated and that the judgment be amended to hold that the appellant bears no liability for infringement.

Changjin Company responded to the appeals of Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company as follows: 1. Regarding the four operas "Chen Sanliang," "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen," "Qingfengting," and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei." To obtain a lawful distribution right for an opera, one must not only obtain the permission of the video producer but also the permission of the script copyright owner and the performers. For the same opera, Changjin Company has obtained the exclusive distribution right. When only the video producer is different, and the appellant holds only the authorization of another video producer without the authorization of the copyright owner and performers of that opera, the publication and distribution of that opera by the appellant is clearly an illegal act that directly harms Changjin Company's economic interests. 2. Regarding "Butterfly Cup." Changjin Company obtained the authorization of Zhang Zhanwei, the copyright owner of the singing melody of that opera; the General Editorial Office of Hebei Television Station has the authority to sign licensing contracts on behalf of Hebei Television Station. The performances of the operas in question, including "Butterfly Cup," are all completed by theaters or troupes, which enjoy the performer's right for the entire opera, not individual actors. The authorization obtained by Changjin Company is complete. 3. The amount of damages awarded by the first-instance court is not improper. In summary, the first-instance court correctly found the facts and applied the law. Changjin Company requests that the appeals be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

Changjin Company responded to the appeal of Tianbao Optical Disc Company as follows: First, the distribution right aims to obtain economic benefits or realize other rights and interests. As long as the appellant's act affects the realization of the right holder's purpose, it constitutes infringement. Second, the "Commission for Reproduction of Audio-Visual Recordings" is only an agreement between the publishing unit and the appellant; whether liability is borne should be determined according to the law. The appellant shares the same address and legal representative as the disc distribution unit, from which it can be inferred that the appellant and other infringers had subjective common intent. Therefore, the appellant should bear joint and several liability with the other infringers for compensation for losses. In summary, Changjin Company requests that the appeal be dismissed and the original judgment be affirmed.

The original defendant, Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, stated the following defense opinion: First, the contract signed between the General Editorial Office of Hebei Television Station and the Theater is lawful and valid. Hebei Television Station, as the producer of the audio-visual recordings of the operas in question, licensed their use to Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, and the Theater further authorized Changjin Company to use them, which complies with legal provisions and contractual terms. Second, Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, as a state-owned performance unit for the relevant operas, organizes and rehearses the performances, reflecting the overall will of the Theater. Its civil liability is borne by the Theater. The Theater enjoys the performer's right and has the right to authorize Changjin Company to reproduce and distribute audio-visual recordings embodying its performances. In summary, Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater did not authorize the appellants to reproduce or distribute the Hebei Bangzi operas in question, and there was no infringement. The original court correctly found the Theater's liability and applied the law. The Theater requests that the original judgment be affirmed.

The original defendant Yinxiangren Company did not submit a written statement of opinion but stated at trial that it had stopped selling the audio-visual products in question.

All parties acknowledged the facts found by the first-instance court, which this Court hereby confirms. Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company claimed that the versions of "Butterfly Cup" distributed by the parties were different, but they acknowledged at trial that both were recorded from the same performance on the same occasion, with only editorial changes and selections made during publication.

Hebei Television Station issued a certificate to this Court stating that it confirms the agreement signed between its General Editorial Office and Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater.

Opinion of the Court: In the first instance, Changjin Company claimed rights over the video recordings of eight operas published and distributed by Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and others, namely "Butterfly Cup," "Chen Sanliang," "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen," "Qingfengting," "Xue Ran Shuang Mei," "Striking the Gold Brick," "Three Strikes on Tao Sanchun," and "Spring Grass Bounces into the Hall." The first-instance court found that Changjin Company had not obtained complete authorization for the last three operas and thus did not support its claims for those three. Since Changjin Company did not appeal, the focus of the dispute in this case is what rights Changjin Company enjoys over the five operas "Butterfly Cup," "Chen Sanliang," "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen," "Qingfengting," and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei," and whether Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House, Tianbao Culture Company, and Tianbao Optical Disc Company infringed its rights and should bear corresponding liability.

1. Regarding the rights enjoyed by Changjin Company

The preparation, organization, rehearsal, etc., of performances of dramatic works are all conducted by performance units such as theaters or troupes, which also bear the required investment. The performance reflects the will of the performance unit. Therefore, for the performance of an entire drama, the performance unit is the performer within the meaning of the Copyright Law and has the right to authorize others to broadcast live or to make sound and video recordings, to reproduce and distribute sound and video recordings, etc. Unless otherwise agreed, individual actors do not enjoy the above rights.

Although the contract signed by the General Editorial Office of Hebei Television Station in its own name with Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater had a defect in subject qualification, since Hebei Television Station has confirmed it, the validity of the contract is not affected. Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater is therefore entitled to authorize Changjin Company to publish and distribute the video recordings produced by Hebei Television Station.

Changjin Company distributed video recordings of "Butterfly Cup," "Chen Sanliang," "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen," "Qingfengting," and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei." For these audio-visual products, it obtained permission from the performance units such as Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater as performers, obtained authorization from the video producer or itself was the video producer, and where there were copyright owners of the script or singing melody, also obtained permission from such copyright owners. The video recordings it distributed comply with Articles 39 and 40 of the Copyright Law of the PRC. For these lawfully produced video recordings, Changjin Company enjoys the rights provided in Article 41 of the Copyright Law of the PRC, including the distribution right.

Changjin Company signed agreements respectively with Hebei Bangzi Opera Theater, Shijiazhuang Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe, and Baoding Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe, obtaining the exclusive right to publish and distribute video recordings of the operas in question. The contract between Changjin Company and Baoding Hebei Bangzi Opera Troupe further expressly stipulates: the Troupe shall no longer record or authorize the recording of that opera for other units. Accordingly, Changjin Company enjoys the exclusive right to publish and distribute video recordings embodying performances of the relevant operas. Others may not infringe without permission.

2. Whether Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company infringed Changjin Company's rights

Among the discs of the operas in question published by Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and distributed by Tianbao Culture Company, the "Butterfly Cup" disc and the video recording distributed by Changjin Company originate from the same recording session. Because Changjin Company enjoys the exclusive distribution right over that video recording, the video recording published and distributed by Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company, although subjected to different editing and selection, still infringed Changjin Company's rights. Their appellate claim that Changjin Company did not obtain complete authorization for "Butterfly Cup" and that they did not infringe lacks factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

Regarding the operas "Chen Sanliang," "Shuang Cuo Yi Hen," "Qingfengting," and "Xue Ran Shuang Mei," the versions distributed by Changjin Company are different from the versions published and distributed by Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company, and they do not originate from the same recording process. According to Article 41 of the Copyright Law, the rights of a video producer are limited to prohibiting others from reproducing or distributing the video recordings produced by that producer without permission; the producer cannot prohibit the reproduction or distribution of video recordings not produced by it. The appellate argument raised by Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company on this point is correct, and this Court supports it. The original judgment erred in finding that Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company infringed Changjin Company's exclusive distribution right over the video recordings solely on the ground that they did not obtain complete authorization. This Court corrects the reasoning. However, as this Court has previously found, in addition to the exclusive distribution right over the video recordings it distributed, Changjin Company also possesses the exclusive right to publish and distribute video recordings of the relevant operas. Without permission and without the permission of the relevant performers, Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company published and distributed video recordings of the relevant operas, thereby infringing Changjin Company's above rights. They should also bear civil liability for ceasing infringement and compensating losses. Although the original judgment's reasoning was improper, its conclusion was correct, and this Court affirms it.

3. Whether Tianbao Optical Disc Company should bear tort liability to Changjin Company

Article 23 of the "Regulations on the Administration of Audio-Visual Products" provides that a unit that reproduces audio-visual products upon commission shall, in accordance with relevant state regulations, verify the commission for reproduction of audio-visual products and the copyright owner's authorization document. Accordingly, if a reproduction unit fails to fully perform the verification obligation under the above administrative regulations and reproduces audio-visual products that infringe upon the lawful rights of others, it shall bear joint tort liability with the producer, publisher, etc., of the infringing audio-visual products. In this case, Tianbao Optical Disc Company only verified the authorization of the lead actors of the operas in question, which clearly did not satisfy the duty of care required by the above regulations. Therefore, the first-instance court's order that it bear joint liability for infringement with Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and Tianbao Culture Company was not improper. Although the "Commission for Reproduction of Audio-Visual Recordings" signed between it and Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House contained provisions on allocation of liability, such provisions are only effective between the two parties and cannot be used to oppose a third party whose rights have been infringed. Tianbao Optical Disc Company's appellate arguments that the duty of care under the "Regulations on the Administration of Audio-Visual Products" is too high and that the "Commission for Reproduction" is not merely a contract between the parties lack legal basis, and this Court does not support them.

4. Whether the amount of damages in the original judgment was reasonable

Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House, Tianbao Culture Company, and Tianbao Optical Disc Company argued that the original judgment's order that they compensate Changjin Company 300,000 yuan was excessive. However, because Changjin Company failed to adduce evidence to prove its actual losses, and Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House and others have also not adduced evidence to prove the profits they obtained from publishing and distributing the discs of the operas in question, and on this basis, considering that this case involves five operas, the time of distribution of the discs by both parties, the nature of the infringing acts, and the reasonable expenses incurred by Changjin Company for this purpose, the original judgment's award of 300,000 yuan is not clearly improper. This Court also does not support this appellate argument by Wenlian Audio-Visual Publishing House, Tianbao Culture Company, and Tianbao Optical Disc Company.

In summary, the original judgment correctly found the facts and reached the correct conclusion, and it should be affirmed. Pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, the judgment is as follows:

Appeal dismissed; original judgment affirmed.

First-instance court acceptance fee of 9,260 yuan: 3,087 yuan to be borne by Guangdong Changjin Audio-Visual Co., Ltd. (already paid); 6,173 yuan to be jointly borne by China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Audio-Visual Publishing House, Tianjin Tianbao Culture Development Co., Ltd., and Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd. (to be paid within 7 days from the effective date of this judgment). Second-instance court acceptance fee of 5,800 yuan: to be jointly borne by China Federation of Literary and Art Circles Audio-Visual Publishing House, Tianjin Tianbao Culture Development Co., Ltd., and Tianjin Tianbao Optical Disc Co., Ltd. (already paid).

This judgment is final.
